Residual: Response evaluations:

Reading this illustration. These curves are numerical approximations to the mean-field equilibrium of a continuous-time game with a menu of three bid levels, subject to remaining budget. Bidding values, budgets, beliefs and rival behavior are solved together. The displayed fixed-point residual measures consistency on the numerical grid; it is not a certified error bound for the continuous-time equilibrium.

Model, regularization and numerical method

Model. The bid menu is {0, 0.04, 0.08}, subject to affordability. Initial budget is 0.08, prior belief is 1/2, and incremental values are 0.060 and 0.095 in the two hidden regimes. The horizon is T = 1, arrival rate λ = 0.6, score-noise scale is 0.20, and the endogenous rival share is 100%. Winning and losing update beliefs. These scenarios have no continuing private-signal diffusion.

Role of temperature. At each state, the policy trades off expected rewards against ε times its KL divergence from a reference distribution. That reference is uniform over the actions the remaining budget can support. A higher temperature increases the weight on staying close to this reference. This is a KL-regularized dynamic game; the state-dependent reference normalization matters.

Gibbs policy. π(a | t, b, p) ∝ ρb(a) exp(Ga(t, b, p; q*)/ε), with probabilities normalized over affordable actions. The score G includes immediate reward and continuation value. The scores and equilibrium flow q* change across the selected temperatures; the displayed curves aggregate these policies over the population.

Why the aggregate shares need not approach one third. Advertisers with different remaining budgets face different affordable menus. Those who exhaust their budget must abstain. Even if every advertiser uses its feasible reference, the population shares generally differ from (1/3, 1/3, 1/3).

Computation. Every selectable temperature was solved separately on 320 time cells and 801 belief nodes by backward optimization, forward population transport and repeated rival-flow updates. The browser displays these saved solutions; it does not rerun the solver. Temperature lines connect computed points to guide the eye. Decision-time shares are drawn as steps; extending the last step to T adds no terminal bidding decision. This is a continuous-time, finite-bid model.

Verification. All 27 marked-flow L¹ residuals are below 7.16 × 10⁻¹², with 6–7 population-response evaluations. The L¹ residual is twice total variation. A residual check does not by itself bound discretization error, and numerical consistency alone is not a proof of equilibrium uniqueness.
